newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba meeting starts with rates still seen on hold.
newsitem.headline: Buba meeting starts with rates still seen on hold.

text.p: The Bundesbank started its regular fortnightly policy-making meeting on Thursday with economists convinced it would keep all interest rates unchanged despite last week's disappointing M3 money supply data.

All 10 economists polled in a Reuter survey said the central bank had no need to change interest rates at present since there was no new convincing evidence that warranted a move in one direction or the other.

A rate increase too soon would choke off what has been an unspectacular recovery this year while Bundesbank officials keep insisting that rates at their current historic lows do not stand in the way of an upturn, economists said.
Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Wednesday he would not rule out another reduction in Bundesbank interest rates in the present economic cycle but added that he did not see one.
May M3 growth, which surprised financial markets by accelerating to 7.0 percent from 6.7 percent in April, was "not nice but not dramatic," Jochimsen told reporters on Wednesday.
He said he saw "with a certain amount of concern" that upward pressures had emerged in import and raw materials prices but added that the increases were not accelerating.

The Bundesbank's main money market rate, the repo rate, has been fixed at 3.00 percent since last August. The discount rate has been set at 2.50 percent and the Lombard rate at 4.50 percent since April 1996.
